QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_71

question.text: Shanti Equity Opportunity Fund (open-ended Cat III) experiences a 20% drawdown. The IM wants to reset HWM to current NAV. What is the CORRECT governance procedure?

answer.text: Reset unilaterally — IM has fee-setting discretion
Reset only for new Class B investors entering post-drawdown
Seek LPAC/majority investor consent AND disclose the reset in LP communication; amend PPM if required

explanation.text: The Logic: HWM reset is an LP-negotiated protection. Any change requires LPAC/majority-investor consent, clear disclosure, and PPM amendment. Unilateral reset would violate fiduciary duty and likely trigger LP litigation/SEBI inspection. The Trap: Option A violates duty. Option C is fictional. Option B discriminates across classes and likely violates MFN clauses. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C (Compliance) for LP consent mechanics; XIX-C for HWM governance. Manager's Pro-Tip: If you anticipate drawdowns (Cat III long-short), build a 'rolling 3-year HWM' mechanic into the PPM from Day 1 — LPs accept this up-front as fair, but resist reset negotiations under duress.
